chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three women may marry in every state: the one who has not yet menstruated, and the like of her who does not menstruate.' I said, 'And what is her limit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When less than nine years have come for her.' And the one who has not been entered into (consummated), and the one who has despaired of menstruation, and the like of her who does not menstruate.' I said, 'And what is her limit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When she is fifty years old.'
ai.seo_question: What are the age limits and conditions for women who do not menstruate regarding marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal criteria for the three categories of women exempt from the standard menstrual waiting period ('iddah) in divorce: pre-pubescent girls (defined as under nine years old), women not yet consummated with, and menopausal women (defined as fifty years old). In Shia jurisprudence, these age thresholds serve as the primary indicators for biological maturity and the cessation of menstruation, thereby determining when a woman is considered 'ready' for marriage and when her 'iddah' concludes immediately upon divorce.
